title: High-cutoff finite harmonic coarse-Schur stress
question: Does the exact two-block harmonic coarse-Schur assembly remain positive at the high oscillator cutoffs already stressed by R-416, with the R-425 beta, orientation, tail and block rules held fixed?

new_perspective.principle: Extend the R-425 harmonic coarse/residual split to the high-cutoff volume-two systems of R-416 while retaining log-domain Gibbs rows and the exact sqrt(pi) projection. This tests whether the finite Schur envelope itself, rather than only the projected graph gap, survives the larger cutoff range.
route: Reuse the hash-pinned R-419 conditional construction, R-416 log-domain rows, R-422 block-mean-zero residual basis and R-425 harmonic split without retuning model parameters.
Evaluate volume two at cutoff dimensions 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 28, 30 and 32 for beta in {1/2,2,8} and both right/left orientations.
Retain every conditional prefix and every support-eligibility boundary; do not turn a high-cutoff sample into a uniform assertion.
Reconstruct the same finite rows in a non-importing lane, reject altered cutoff/parent/scope inputs, and compile the scalar Lean bookkeeping cross-check.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: Persistence of the finite harmonic envelope sharpens the analytic target; it does not prove a cutoff-uniform common-core estimate, history transfer, OS/KMS/GNS coercivity, a sector gap, or a continuum limit.

finite_theorem.space: For each admitted conditional row, the positive sqrt(pi)-transformed graph is split into two block-constant modes and their orthogonal complement.
finite_theorem.harmonic_schur: The residual complement is eliminated by the exact finite Schur solve S=A_UU-A_UV A_VV^(-1) A_VU.
finite_theorem.residual: The residual gap is recomputed with the R-422 block-mean-zero basis and compared with the harmonic residual block.
finite_theorem.combined_lower_envelope: The checked finite envelope is 0.5*min(coarse Schur gap,residual gap).
finite_theorem.stress_interpretation: The high-cutoff stress is stopped at the first declared residual-reuse disagreement; no positive Schur envelope is promoted beyond the rows checked before that route-local failure.

failure_contract.reason: At a declared high-cutoff row the R-422 residual gap and a separately reconstructed direct residual gap disagree beyond the preregistered comparison tolerance.

lean_crosscheck.role: R426 checks only scalar envelope and high-cutoff grid bookkeeping; Python carries the matrix and Gibbs-row evidence.

assumptions: The hash-pinned R-419 conditional law is positive and normalized and its projected momentum conductance is symmetric and nonnegative.
The R-416 log-domain reconstruction and R-422 sqrt(pi) residual basis apply at every listed finite cutoff.
Beta values, orientations, alpha=1/40, tail threshold four, probability floor and gap floor are fixed across the stress.
Every admitted block has at least two core and two tail coordinates and a positive residual block before the harmonic solve.
Declared numerical tolerances are comparison thresholds only and lower bounds are never rounded upward.
missing_assumptions: A cutoff-, volume-, phase- and exhaustion-uniform lower bound for the coarse Schur and residual forms on one Hamiltonian common core.
A common split-limit map and two-sided form control as the oscillator cutoff is removed.
Uniform control of actual R-399 histories and transfer through the R-415 semigroup interface.
Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS/GNS identification, physical-sector projection and a sectorwise coercive estimate.
promotion_criteria: Prove an analytic Schur/residual estimate on a domain-controlled unbounded Q3 common core.
Establish a positive envelope uniform in cutoff, volume, phase and exhaustion rather than only on this high-cutoff sample.
Transfer that envelope through the history and OS/KMS/GNS interfaces before any sector or physical promotion.
stop_conditions: A singular residual block, nonpositive Schur gap or independent disagreement stops this high-cutoff lane and is retained as a finite construction failure.
A residual-reuse difference above the fixed comparison tolerance stops the lane; the tolerance must not be relaxed or hidden by clipping.
A collapse of the finite combined envelope is recorded without clipping and does not imply physical gaplessness.
Finite stress positivity cannot be promoted to a common-core, GNS, continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
evidence_level: T0 / executed high-cutoff finite stress with a declared route-local residual-reuse failure; no uniform theorem or physical conclusion
non_claims: No accepted high-cutoff Schur or residual-reuse closure after the route-local failure.
No cutoff-, volume-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform coarse or residual bound.
No global Poincare theorem, common Hamiltonian core or common split-limit map.
No history transfer, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction or sectorwise gap.
No continuum, C6, Sector-A, Pre-A, Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
boundary: R-426 is a finite high-cutoff stress of the R-425 harmonic Schur assembly at volume two. It stops at the declared V=2, d=16, beta=8, right-orientation residual-reuse mismatch and records a route-local finite construction failure; it does not close the Q3LOCK parent gates.
next_unlock: Reconcile the independently reconstructed residual basis with the R-422 harmonic residual at high cutoff using a declared precision/basis convention, then rerun without changing the comparison tolerance before attempting any analytic common-core estimate.
no_overclaim: The route-local numerical mismatch is not a physical no-go theorem. It does not imply gaplessness, regulator dependence of the theory, or any Yang-Mills or mass-gap conclusion.
